explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Measuring the waters in a hand, spanning the heavens and weighing mountains on a scale is a job with one name on it. The prophet asks the questions, and nobody else steps forward. I can't even weigh a cookie box without it tipping over, so I'll leave the mountains to God.

Solomon, David's son, did sit on his father's throne as Israel's king (1 Kings 2:12). But the prophet names no king in these questions. Later in this passage he says God brings princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless (Isaiah 40:23). So the one measuring the waters and weighing the hills is God alone.

David was the shepherd who became Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and that's a big résumé. Still, the prophet never names him in these questions. Nobody has held the dust of the earth in a basket, not even a king. Honestly, I'd need a much bigger basket and a lot of help just to try.

Not quite, friend. The text says the opposite. The prophet asks, “Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice?” and nobody steps up to answer. Nobody taught Him, so there's no teacher in the room.

You got it, baker. The prophet asks who taught God the paths of justice and who showed Him the way of understanding, and no hand goes up. God didn't need a teacher. I needed three tries and a very patient Mother Miller to learn how to lift a cookie straight.

explanations.answer: Like a drop in a bucket
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The prophet says the nations are like a drop in a bucket, a speck of dust on the scales. That's a very small drop next to a very big God. Nobody notices one drop when the bucket is full.

A flood is big and loud, and the prophet goes the other way. He says the nations are like a drop in a bucket. Right next to that, he calls them a speck of dust on the scales. Not much roaring from a speck.

A mountain feels like a safe guess, but the prophet already put mountains on a scale in verse 12. God weighs them. The nations are the small things here, like a drop in a bucket. If mountains fit on God's scale, a nation is a crumb.

Not this time, friend. The prophet says Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering. Lebanon was known for its cedars (1 Kings 5:6), so that's a lot of wood. Even all of it wouldn't be enough.

You got it, baker. The prophet says Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering. Lebanon was famous for its cedars (1 Kings 5:6). Even that whole forest falls short, and my little oven would give up long before it did.

That's right. The one who can't afford gold and silver chooses wood that will not rot. Then he goes looking for a skilled craftsman. That's a lot of planning for something that has to be set up by hand.

Bronze is a good guess, but the prophet doesn't mention it here. The first idol is covered in gold and fitted with silver chains. The person who can't manage that chooses wood that will not rot. Bronze never makes the list.

Stone sounds sturdy, but it isn't what the prophet says. The text says this person chooses wood that will not rot. The gold and silver belong to the fancier idol. Stone from the hillside isn't in the passage at all.

You got it, baker. The man seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple. So he hires a professional to make sure his idol stays upright. That's a lot of effort for something that needs help standing.

Close, but the text says it plainly. He seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple. So the man doesn't stop at choosing the wood. He also goes and finds an expert so the thing stays standing.

explanations.answer: Above the circle of the earth
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The prophet says He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth. That's a view from way up high. Nothing down here is too far from His sight.
The Jordan is a real river, but the prophet doesn't put God beside it. He says God sits enthroned above the circle of the earth. That's a lot higher than any riverbank. It's a much bigger seat.

Gold has been on the brain since the idols, friend. But the prophet doesn't place God in a temple here. He says He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth. That's the whole earth, seen from above.
You got it, baker. From where God sits, the dwellers of the earth are like grasshoppers. That's how far up His seat is. Nobody down here is looking down on anybody.

Giants is the opposite direction, friend. The prophet says the earth's dwellers are like grasshoppers from where God sits. He's making people small to show how great God is. A giant would be a bigger problem for the point.

Cedars are tall and proud, so I see the thinking. But the text says the dwellers of the earth are like grasshoppers. That's a small, hopping bug, not a tree. It's about as far from a cedar as you can get.

That's right, baker. A whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble. Those are the dry leftovers after a harvest, and a whirlwind carries them off without any trouble. That's how easily the rulers of the earth are swept away.
Smoke drifts off fast, so I get it. But the prophet says a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble. Stubble is what's left standing in a field after the grain is gone. Smoke isn't in this verse.
Sand does blow around, friend. But the verse says a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble. That's dry stalks, not grains. Sand is a nice guess that just isn't in the text.

explanations.answer: He calls each one by name
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. He leads forth the starry host by number and calls each one by name. Every star is counted and every star has a name. I only name my toppings, and that's already a lot of work.

explanations.answer: He gives each one a season
explanations.explanation: That sounds nice, but it isn't what the prophet says. He says God leads forth the starry host by number and calls each one by name. Seasons never come up. Names do.

explanations.answer: He hides each one by day
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention hiding stars at all, friend. It says God leads forth the starry host by number and calls each one by name. That's the part to hold on to. Every star is known.

You got it, baker. The prophet says that because of God's great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing. Every star is counted and every star is there. Count them all you like, you won't find a gap.
Not this time, friend. The prophet says that because of His great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing. No empty spots in the sky. Every star shows up.

explanations.answer: Their way is hidden from Him
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jacob and Israel say, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God.” That's their complaint, and the prophet answers it right away. I know that feeling a little. I sat in a junk drawer for years thinking nobody remembered me.

explanations.answer: He is angry with them forever
explanations.explanation: That isn't what they say, friend. Their words are, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God.” Anger never comes up. They say their way is hidden from Him.

Nope, they never say that. What they say is, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God.” There's no other nation in their complaint. The prophet answers what they actually said.
Not quite, friend. The text says the opposite. The prophet says the LORD is the everlasting God and that He will not grow tired or weary. He doesn't run out, and no snooze button is needed.
You got it, baker. The everlasting God will not grow tired or weary. I get tired after one batch, and my mustache gets tired before I do. He doesn't.

explanations.answer: No one can search it out
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The prophet says His understanding is beyond searching out. You can dig as long as you like and never reach the bottom. That's a good thing to know when you don't understand His ways.

explanations.answer: Only the priests can learn it
explanations.explanation: The prophet doesn't say that, friend. He says His understanding is beyond searching out. That means nobody gets to the bottom of it. It isn't saved for one group.
Growing sounds reasonable, but the text doesn't say it. The prophet says His understanding is beyond searching out. Something that grows started smaller. This one has no bottom to find.
You got it, baker. The LORD gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak. He gives to the ones who are running out. I know a few mornings like that.

The mighty are fine on their own, so I see the guess. But the verse says the LORD gives power to the faint. It's the faint and the weak who get the strength. The text speaks to the ones who are running low.
That isn't what the verse says, friend. The LORD gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak. The proud aren't mentioned. Strength goes to the ones who are low on it.

explanations.answer: Those who wait upon the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength. Even the strong grow tired, so waiting on Him is the way. I'm still learning that one, since I've never been good at waiting for the oven timer.

explanations.answer: Those who bring gifts to the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's a kind thought, friend. But the prophet says it's those who wait upon the LORD who will renew their strength. Gifts aren't mentioned in the verse. The word is waiting.

explanations.answer: Those who fast before the LORD
explanations.explanation: The verse doesn't mention fasting, friend. The prophet says those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength. That's the one thing he points to. Waiting upon Him is the answer.
You got it, baker. Those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary. Think of running without ever running out of steam. That's more than I manage on my best day.
Not this time, friend. The prophet says those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary. They'll walk and not faint too. It's a promise from the prophet, and it's a good one.
